candidates.name: Nowa Huta Museum
candidates.alt: formerly the People's Republic of Poland Museum
candidates.content: An interesting look into Nowa Huta during the Communist era. Changing exhibitions on the top floor, civil defense shelter turned museum in the basement,

candidates.name: Polish Aviation Museum
candidates.content: A museum consisting of a new pavilion (good contemporary architecture) and few hangars filled with over two hundred historic gliders, aircraft, helicopters and more. Among them is a collection of 22 extremely rare antique planes t

candidates.name: Old Synagogue
candidates.price: Adults: 18 zł, discounted: 14 zł, free on Mondays
candidates.content: Built in the 15th century, the synagogue is the oldest still standing in Poland. It was ransacked by the Nazis during World War II and was renovated between 1956 and 1959. It is now as a museum documenting Jewish life in Kraków.

candidates.name: Divine Mercy Sanctuary
candidates.content: A popular destination for religious pilgrimages to Kraków. The basilica was built between 1999 and 2002. You can climb the tower of the sanctuary and enjoy views over the southern parts of Kraków.

candidates.name: Museum of City Engineering
candidates.content: It is in old tram sheds and on the grounds of a former gasworks and power plant. It has exhibitions on the history of Polish automotive, public transportation, radio and television, household and office appliances industries. The

candidates.name: Galicia Jewish Museum
candidates.price: Tickets are 15 zł or 8 zł with a student discount
candidates.hours: Daily 10:00-18:00 Closed on Yom Kippur and Christmas Day
candidates.content: Houses an exhibition of photographs with explanations in Polish and English. These are recent photographs of locations around Poland associated with the Holocaust. Some are places where massacres occurred; most show old synagogues

candidates.name: Remuh Synagogue
candidates.hours: Sun-Fri 09:00-18:00 Closed to the public on Saturdays and Jewish holidays
candidates.content: The synagogue and adjoining Jewish Cemetery with the grave of Moses Isserles.

candidates.name: Tempel Synagogue
candidates.content: Built in 1860 - 1862. Reform synagogue that is open to the public. Since it's an operational synagogue, men and women should dress somewhat conservatively and have their shoulders covered. During the Nazi occupation, the synagogue

candidates.name: Wawel Cathedral
candidates.content: Known in full as Królewska Bazylika Archikatedralna śś. Stanisława i Wacława na Wawelu, or the "Royal Archcathedral Basilica of Saints Stanislaus and Wenceslaus on Wawel Hill". On 2 Nov 1946 a talented young priest called Karol Wo

candidates.name: Princes Czartoryski Museum
candidates.price: Adult 35 zł, conc 20 zł, Tuesday free
candidates.content: Branch of the National Museum, re-opened in Dec 2019 after refurbishment. Classical art, the highlight being the Mona Weasel, an authentic Leonardo da Vinci portrait, in Polish Dama z gronostajem. She's properly called "The Lady w

candidates.name: Cloth Hall
candidates.price: Gallery adult 25 zł, conc 15 zł, free on Sun
candidates.content: In the centre of the square, this large trading hall was built in Gothic style in the 14th century and rebuilt in Renaissance style in the 16th. The ground floor is an arcade filled with souvenir shops: this is open 24 hours even

candidates.name: Town Hall Tower
candidates.content: Most of the Gothic / Renaissance Town Hall was demolished in 1820, but the tower survives, now a branch of the City Museum. You can climb to the observation deck on the top floor, and peer into the workings of the clock, now radio

candidates.name: St Mary's Basilica
candidates.hours: Mon-Sat 12:00-18:00, Sun 14:00-18:00, no visits during Mass
candidates.content: Built in Gothic Brick from the 14th C, with two unequal towers facing the main square. The hejnał is played from the towers every hour and on Polish Radio at noon, commemorating the trumpeter slain as he sounded the alarm. There's

candidates.name: MOCAK
candidates.content: One of the newest museums in Krakow, located in renovated buildings belonging to the former Schindler’s Factory, houses a permanent collection and temporary exhibitions of modern art, sometimes the 'I don't get it' kind. Inside a

candidates.name: Schindler's Enamel Factory
candidates.price: 36 zł, reduced 32 zł. Mondays limited amount of free tickets
candidates.hours: Mon 10:00-14:00, Tue-Thu 09:00-19:00 Fri-Sun 09:00-20:00, closed on first Tue of the month
candidates.content: Museum houses a permanent exhibition concerning Krakow under Nazi occupation; it is located in the administrative building of the former Schindler's Factory.

candidates.name: Under the Eagle Pharmacy
candidates.content: Exhibition focuses on the pharmacist - Tadeusz Pankiewicz, a Righteous among the Nations and life in Jewish Ghetto and Plaszow camp. Museum was renovated as memory lab and expanded in March 2013.

candidates.name: The Benedictine Abbey in Tyniec
candidates.price: Visit the abbey with a guide: 6zł. Museum: 7zł normal ticket, 5zł reduced ticket
candidates.content: St. Peter's and St. Paul's Church and Benedictine Abbey are situated at the bank of Vistula river. In the 11th century it was one of the most important scientific places in the first Polish Kingdom, the first chronicles of Poland

candidates.name: National Museum in Krakow - Main Building
candidates.alt: Muzeum Narodowe w Krakowie - Gmach Główny
candidates.price: Adult 35 zł, conc 25 zł, Sundays free
candidates.content: The permanent collection comprises 20th-Century Polish Art, Decorative Art, and Arms and Uniforms in Poland. The ground floor has temporary exhibitions

candidates.name: Museum of Photography Strzelnica branch
candidates.content: Permanent collection shows works of Polish photographers from 1850 to WW2. Several temporary exhibitions a year on both documentary and art photography.

candidates.name: Jan Matejko Manor
candidates.content: Summer residence of one of the most well known Polish artists - Jan Matejko. Today a museum.

candidates.name: St. Venceslaus' Church and Cistercian Abbey
candidates.content: Built in 1266 by the bishop Prandota for the Cistercians who came to Mogila in 1220 invited by duke Leszek the White and bishop Iwo Odrowaz. The crossway was founded by Casimir the Great in the 14th century. The interior is painte

candidates.name: Ethnographic Museum
candidates.price: Regular 18 zł. Reduced 10 zł. Free on Sunday
candidates.content: Located in the 15th-century Kazimierz town hall.

candidates.name: Centre for Jewish Culture
candidates.content: Exhibitions, concerts, seminars and workshops on Jewish culture. There is also a cafe with a roof terrace and a great antiquarian bookshop in the basement.

candidates.name: Bne Emuna Synagogue
candidates.content: The building of Judaica Foundation – Centre For Jewish Culture. Formerly a prayer house, now primarily used by the centre.

candidates.name: Chewra Thilim Synagogue
candidates.content: Historically a prayer house, today an exhibition space and the location of HEVRE Bar. Features rare, well-preserved polychrome.

candidates.name: Mizrachi Synagogue
candidates.content: Built in 1930s right next to Izaak Synagogue. Since the 80s it has served as a Jewish Culture Centre.

candidates.name: Corpus Christi Church
candidates.content: Gothic Church erected by Kazimierz the Great in 1340. The greatest Italian artist of the Renaissance, Bartholomaeo Berrecci, is buried here. The interior is baroque with a marvelous, high baroque altar and maybe the most beautiful

candidates.name: St. Catherine's Church
candidates.content: Gothic Church erected by Kazimierz the Great in 1363 for the Augustinian Order. There is a beautiful baroque altar and the Renaissance grave of bishop Spytek Jordan inside the church.

candidates.name: Jewish Culture Festival
candidates.content: A classic, one of the biggest Jewish culture festivals in the world. A week of tours, concerts, workshops on cuisine, dance, music and calligraphy topped with a huge final show on Saturday evening. June/July

candidates.name: Krakow Film Festival
candidates.content: One of the oldest film events dedicated to documentary, animated and short fiction films in Europe. In a week over 200 films are shown in around six cinemas (10 screens) around the city and in an open air one next to Wawel castle.

candidates.name: Wianki
candidates.content: St. John's Night (Midsummer) celebration. An evening of concerts finished with a fireworks show taking place on Vistula river banks next to Wawel castle. A booze-up. June

candidates.name: Off Camera
candidates.content: International festival of independent cinema. April

candidates.name: Etiuda and Anima
candidates.content: International film festival built around animations and short films. November

candidates.name: Photomonth
candidates.content: One month long festival with around forty different photography exhibitions around the city. May

candidates.name: Live Music Festival
candidates.content: Typical summer open air music fest. Stars that appeared past years include: Kanye West, Muse, The Chemical Brothers, 50 Cent.

candidates.name: Sacrum Profanum
candidates.content: Music fest with concerts of such stars as Steve Reich, Aphex Twin or Kraftwerk taking place in unusual places like churches, museums and factories.

candidates.name: Unsound
candidates.content: World-renowned experimental music and art event. October

candidates.name: Krakowskie Noce
candidates.content: Five nights (one in each month from May to September): Night of Museums (free museums), Night of Theatres (free theatres), Night of Jazz (free jazz concerts), Cracovia Sacra Night (free concerts of church music) and Night of Poetr

candidates.name: Spółdzielnia Ogniwo
candidates.content: Leftist cafe, bar, bookstore and culture house owned and managed by a cooperative. They organize many events: discussions, film screenings, exhibitions and book promotions. Prices at the bar are pretty low. Books they sell are mos

candidates.name: Bajit Chadasz
candidates.content: Jewish culture festival, organised by Jewish Cultural Centre in Kazimierz with concerts, exhibitions and lectures.

candidates.name: Krakow Valley Golf & Country Club
candidates.content: Also a hotel, shooting range and horse rides.

candidates.name: Royal Kraków Golf & Country Club
candidates.content: Between Wieliczka and Niepołomice. Also a hotel.

candidates.name: Nowa Huta Lake
candidates.content: Artificial water reservoir right next to Huta centre. Place for sports, rollerskating, a sunbath and swan feeding (don't do the last one, it's forbidden).

candidates.name: Com-Com Zone
candidates.price: Swimming pool 12/9 zł, halls & gym & sauna 20 zł
candidates.content: Sport centre close to Hutnik stadium: training halls, football pitches, climbing wall, swimming pool, sauna.

candidates.name: Waterpark
candidates.content: Indoor pool with slides, children's pool and padding area, plus sauna.

candidates.name: Juliusz Słowacki Theatre
candidates.content: Grand old venue by north city walls stages concerts, plays and other events.

candidates.name: Małopolski Ogród Sztuki
candidates.content: Multifunctional space for plays, exhibitions and concerts.

candidates.name: Kika Cinema
candidates.content: A cinema and a cafe. Arthouse, European films, classics, showings for children.

candidates.name: Alchemia
candidates.content: Very popular, they defined the "Kazimierz style" years ago which is so unmistakable that videoclips are being shot there. There are sometimes concerts or film screenings in the underground room.

candidates.name: Omerta
candidates.content: Disregard the mafia theme, what matters is 13 types of beer on tap and dozens more in bottles! Hard to find a place in the evenings. Located in the same building as Coca.

candidates.name: Stara Zajezdnia
candidates.content: Former tram depot, later go-kart track where Polish F1 driver Robert Kubica trained as a kid. Now a huge bierhalle with a restaurant with own minibrewery. Several types of beer and whisky and sport events transmitted on few big sc

candidates.name: Ambasada Śledzia
candidates.content: Nice outside patio and interesting interior with poetry scrawled on the walls. Polish tapas at 4 zł a dish, drinks 6 zł and mains. Knock back vodka and herring and enjoy.

candidates.name: Pierwszy Lokal na Stolarskiej po lewej stronie idąc od Małego Rynku
candidates.alt: The First Place on the Left Side of Stolarska if You Come from Small Square
candidates.content: Best name ever! They have good beer on tap called Smocza Głowa (Dragon's Head) which is made locally and hard to get. Most areas are for smokers, limited seating for non-smokers.

candidates.name: Klub Kombinator
candidates.content: coffee, beer, vodka and board games. open till midnight.

candidates.name: Absynt
candidates.content: "Kazimierz style" bar which looks like old flat. They serve unique drinks with absinthe.

candidates.name: Craftownia
candidates.content: An brewpub with an excellent selection of Polish craft beers.

candidates.name: Eszeweria
candidates.content: Old pub with a nice small garden in the back.

candidates.name: Hevre
candidates.content: Located in the old house of prayer this place exactly presents "Kazimierz style". Also listed in the See section as Chewra Thilim Synagogue.

candidates.name: Kolanko no 6
candidates.content: Another example of Kazimierz style. A bar with concerts and film screenings perfect for an evening drink or an afternoon coffee.

candidates.name: La Habana
candidates.content: A bar with Cuban atmosphere, refreshing beer - juice cocktails, Hemingway's favourite drinks and some light snacks.

candidates.name: Le Scandale
candidates.content: A huge selection of drinks with a great atmosphere.

candidates.name: Mleczarnia
candidates.content: Typical Kazimierz place with chairs and tables found on the attic. Very nice courtyard beer garden in summer.

candidates.name: Judah Food Market
candidates.content: Street food market with 11 trucks: Knitted coffee, zapiekanki, Belgian fries, chimney cakes, kumpir (baked potatoes), Andrus Maczanka po Krakowsku, Pierogy, Azjem (Asian), burgers, tempura, hot dogs.

candidates.name: Zakaski i Wodka
candidates.content: This is a great example of an old fashioned Polish bar: such bars serve more food than a bar in western Europe, so it is a place to both eat and drink. You can buy sour soup or hunter's soup with pickled gherkins or bread and pork

candidates.name: Hariprasad Samosa & Curry
candidates.content: Vegan Indian food. Very small: only seats about 6. Stunningly good food. Seems to be a lunchtime place.

candidates.name: Marchewka z Groszkiem
candidates.price: Soups 10-17 zł, most mains 25-45 zł without sides
candidates.content: Ok traditional Polish cuisine. Can get crowded.

candidates.name: Restauracja Cechowa
candidates.content: Serves good traditional Polish food at reasonable prices in the middle of the old town. It may be difficult to get good value food in the old town, but this restaurant proves it's not impossible.

candidates.name: U Babci Maliny
candidates.content: The name means "At Grandma Raspberry's": cheap authentic Polish food. The branch at Sławkowska is self-service, with communal seating at long wooden tables and benches. Order at the counter (English menus available), then listen f

candidates.name: Wierzynek
candidates.content: Upscale traditional cuisine in one of the oldest restaurants in Poland. Mikołaj Wierzynek invited several kings and the German Emperor in 1364 to a feast there and gave them the golden dishes they ate from.

candidates.name: Jadłodajnia Wczoraj i Dziś
candidates.content: That translates as "Eating place yesterday & today" so they're aiming for communist-era. Canteen with self-service, good budget Polish meals, no alcohol.

candidates.name: Bar Północny
candidates.content: Typical local milk bar. See milk bars.

candidates.name: Stylowa
candidates.content: Located close to the Central Square, the self-proclaimed "Stylish" dates back to 1956, when it opened as the first restaurant in Nowa Huta. The interior was lightly remodeled in the 2000s, but the place remains largely a time caps

candidates.name: Bagelmama
candidates.content: Bagels, soups, salads, wraps.

candidates.name: Coca
candidates.content: Very small place with Sicilian fast food. Ice cream in summer.

candidates.name: Galeria Kazimierz
candidates.content: A big mall next to Kazimierz district. Over a hundred stores with clothes, shoes, furniture, books, etc. Also in the complex food market and Cinema City multiplex.

december.text: The communist government collapsed in 1989 and Kraków has undergone another period of regeneration, with historic buildings being restored, but many of the dull post-war buildings still remain. In the 21st century, especially with the advent of budget airlines, Kraków has become one of the most popular destinations in
Take part in a city game which combines sightseeing of the city with adventure, integration and fun. You'll find them advertised in hostels.
Christmas Market: this is the oldest such market in Poland, held from the end of November to the end of December in Main Market Square.
Grzaniec, mulled wine with cloves and other spices, very popular around Christmas when sold on Market Square.
Nowa Huta Lake: Artificial water reservoir right next to Huta centre. Place for sports, rollerskating, a sunbath and swan feeding (don't do the last one, it's forbidden).

Krzysztofory Palace: The main building. Usual historical museum stuff: armour, swords, etc. Every year after Christmas there is an exhibition concerning local tradition: Krakow szopka (characteristic nativity scene where historical buildings of Kraków are used as backdrop for the Nativity of Jesus.)
